questions.q: Why is My Domain described as a hard prerequisite for most identity features in this course?
options: It is purely cosmetic and not actually required for anything else
SSO, Identity Provider setup, and Auth. Providers all need a unique, org-specific URL to anchor certificates, Entity IDs, and callback URLs to
It is only required for Experience Cloud sites
It replaces the need for a Connected App entirely
questions.explain: My Domain gives the org a unique, stable subdomain that other identity features depend on as their anchor for certificates, Entity IDs, and callback URLs — without it, those features have nothing stable to configure against.

questions.q: What is the final step in the My Domain registration process that actually changes the org's login URL for everyone?
options: Check Availability
Register Domain
Deploy to Users
Login Page Branding
questions.explain: Deploy to Users is the point where the new domain becomes the org's actual login URL for all users — the step that should only happen after thorough testing.

questions.q: Where would an admin go to make a configured social sign-on Auth. Provider appear as a clickable button on the login page?
options: Session Settings
Login Page Branding (under My Domain)
Permission Set Groups
Data Export
questions.explain: Login Page Branding, reached from the My Domain page, is where admins customize which authentication options (including configured Auth. Providers) actually appear on the login page.

questions.q: What should happen before an admin clicks 'Deploy to Users' on a newly registered My Domain?
options: Nothing; it can be deployed immediately with no testing
Thorough testing, including confirming logins, custom links, and bookmarks still resolve correctly
All users must be deactivated first
The org must switch to Salesforce Classic
questions.explain: Because deploying changes the org's actual login URL for everyone, testing beforehand catches broken bookmarks, links, or integrations before they affect every user.

questions.q: If an architect finds an org that hasn't enabled My Domain yet while reviewing an identity architecture, how should that be treated?
options: As an unimportant cosmetic gap to fix later
As a blocking finding, since nearly all SSO and Identity Provider features in this course depend on My Domain being enabled first
As irrelevant, since My Domain only affects branding
As something only relevant to Experience Cloud orgs
questions.explain: Because SSO, Identity Provider setup, and Auth. Providers all assume My Domain already exists, an org missing it has a foundational gap that blocks nearly every other identity feature.
